metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [12. Januar 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.83

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [12. Januar 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.83
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.83
- Datum: 12.1.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
12. January 1941 Dear Manfred and Hannah, we got today your
letter from the 18. Dec. and soon you will have news about Eva. We
are flying the 15 th to Bahia, Recife, Belem in the North of Brazil
for six days
and this part (nearly the half way) is paid to us, so that we have
only the other half on our own account; you see we manage things
all right and as I have nearly finished the book on Brazil, I can
always rely upon the people here and I hope, that if for Tristental
the Argentine visa should not work - the consul had not only one
cable to deliver a tourist visa to him but two - I can try to get it here
for him as a special favour. Now to Eva. We will stay about three to
four month in the States and of cause our first idea was to take her
here with us, but I am afraid that it is not possible as we will be often in
town till late at night and has to leave her alone. But I think we will
find someone, if she would like a change - all this has to be in-
vestigated {meanwhile} sure place[?]. Should we go back to Rio the question would arise
to take her with us. Here all is much easier and we could take a
flat or little house, the only difficulty is school. There are good English
or American colleges here, but it exists the obligation, that all schools
have to teach (mostly) in Portuguese and she had to learn a new language
still and a language which is not so important as French or Spanish.
But it is still much to early to make plans as we ourselves have not
yet decided - who can make decisions beforehand in such times?
In any case, please rely upon us, that we will do our best and not
only for yours sake but because we love both Eva and know how impor-
tant these years of development are. My sister-in-law wrote that she
did send Christmas presents to her and to the little boy, without to get
a single word of reply and also to us Salmons never answered and you
may imagine that we wrote to these stupid people in the most kindest way.
You understand, that we do not like the idea that Eva should be
educated by people who are lacking themselves of the faintest
notion of manners. But please do not worry about all this and

pages.transcription:
2)
remember always that she is safe and you have not to be exited[?]
about every alarm while she would be in school or out of the house
in England. I am more concerned about you, that you have too much
to do and not enough time for rest, let us hope that the worst is
over, here everybody is convinced of the British-American final success and
then all our pains and losses would be no more without sense - it
would be again a world to live within. When this beast Hitler should
be definitively overthrown, no price would be too high.
We are somewhat tired and glad to come out of the heat. The weather
is splendid, the town beautiful, but we have both the feeling, that a
little winter will do us good. Myself I feel, that I have to retire
somewhere to do quickly my work and not to see more people -
I believe we have been on this voyage six hundred to six thousand
and I do not know more, what language I am speaking and this
is a heavy strain. We hope to be the 23 or 24 at the Wyndham Hotel
42 West 58 Street but only for a week and you will have our
adress by cable (please cable always with reply) In any case letters
or communications will reach us c/o Viking Press 18 East 48 Street.
Love to Martha and all others and ever yours Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf rosa Papier. Die Tinte ist violett. 'everybody' wurde über 'all' eingefügt.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Natur und der violetten Tinte auf rosa Papier. Einige Wörter sind aufgrund der Kursivschrift leicht interpretativ, aber im Kontext eindeutig.
